What Is an Open-Source VPN?
An open-source VPN makes its source code available to the public. Users, researchers, and security experts can check how it works and how it matches up with the provider's claims.
PIA is one of the few VPN providers with reviewable source code. We publish the code for all our VPN apps in our GitHub repository, so anyone can see exactly how the technology works. Transparency earns trust, not promises.
Why Transparency Matters in Open-Source VPNs
When you’re trusting a VPN provider with your personal browsing data, transparency is essential. The more you can verify for yourself, the less you have to take a VPN provider’s word for it. That's why PIA pairs open-source apps with an independently audited No-Logs policy and quarterly transparency reports, giving you multiple ways to check our technology and privacy practices.
When you inspect PIA VPN’s open-source code, you can verify how our apps handle your traffic, confirm there are no hidden vulnerabilities or trackers, and review updates as we publish them.
Get PIA VPN
Open-Source VPN Protocols
Open source doesn't stop at our apps. PIA supports both OpenVPN and WireGuard, two of the most trusted open-source protocols. This means the technology that encrypts and routes your traffic can be independently reviewed, too.
WireGuard
WireGuard delivers fast speeds. Its lightweight design makes it well suited to bandwidth-heavy tasks like streaming, video calling, downloading, and gaming.
What makes it stand out:
Easier to review and audit with a compact codebase of around only 4,000 lines
Strong, modern security from Curve25519 key exchange and ChaCha20 encryption
Reconnects quickly when you switch networks thanks to fast handshakes
OpenVPN
OpenVPN’s configurable design makes it a great choice for users who want greater control over their VPN connection, with reliable performance across different networks and devices.
What makes it stand out:
Long-established codebase extensively reviewed by security researchers
Supports strong AES-256 encryption with robust authentication
Customizable to different security and network requirements
Why Choose PIA as Your Open-Source VPN
Customization Options
Get the right balance of performance and privacy with your choice of protocols, adjustable encryption settings, and Multi-Hop feature.
RAM-Only Infrastructure
We can’t store anything on our RAM-only network as our servers wipe all browsing data on every reboot.
Advanced Security
Reduce exposure on unstable Wi-Fi with a Kill Switch, plus built-in leak protection that helps prevent IP and DNS leaks.
113-Country Network
Get the IP address you need in a couple of clicks with PIA’s global network spanning 180 locations, including all 50 US states.
Fast Speeds
Stream, game, and download updates on a fast and reliable connection through PIA’s high-performance 10-Gbps server network.
24/7 Live Support
Get answers to your questions any time you need them from our friendly support team, available via live chat and email.
Get PIA VPN
Secure All Your Devices With Proven Privacy
PIA VPN has apps for most popular operating systems, including Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, and Android – and there’s no limit to the number of devices you can connect to at one time. To add protection to your network, configure PIA VPN on a compatible router to secure game consoles, smart TVs, and other gadgets that lack native VPN support.

FAQ
What does open source mean?
Open source means that the source code for a given piece of software is available to inspect and review. PIA publishes the source code for its VPN apps on GitHub, making it available for anyone to examine how they work.
Why is open source important?
Open-source software can be independently reviewed, creating transparency around how certain products work. For a VPN, this helps build trust and allows researchers and other experts to examine how the software works and report any vulnerabilities they find, making the software more secure over time.
Why should I trust Private Internet Access?
PIA invites trust through our commitment to transparency, but you don't have to take our word for it when it comes to your privacy. Our app code is available for public inspection on GitHub, our No-Logs policy has undergone independent reviews, we publish quarterly transparency reports, and use widely adopted open-source protocols.
Is an open-source VPN more secure?
An open-source VPN offers an important security advantage: transparency and auditability. Anyone with the relevant expertise can inspect the code, identify potential vulnerabilities, and verify how the VPN implements its security features. However, that doesn’t make it more secure. It still needs to be maintained, tested, and reviewed.
Where can I view PIA’s open-source code?
You can view PIA’s open-source VPN app code on GitHub, where we publish and regularly update the source code across all supported platforms.
Can I get a free open-source VPN?
Yes, some open-source VPNs offer free options, but free VPNs may come with trade-offs such as fewer server locations, data caps, or limited customer support. PIA is a premium open-source VPN starting at only [PS_PRICE] per month for long-term plans. We offer 180 server locations, unlimited VPN bandwidth, and 24/7 live chat and email support.
